observed_vs_expected: Expected best_target_score to increase relative to route_01’s 0.5152 baseline, but actual score dropped from 0.62027 (round 1) to 0.44016 (round 2). Expected tightest_margin stability held (0.6256), confirming margins were not the bottleneck. The decrease directly validates the false-hypothesis expectation that optimal thickness lies outside the newly narrowed bounds.
deviation_mechanism: Constraining layer thicknesses to tighter tolerances forced the optimizer to operate away from the integer-half-wavelength optical path lengths required for the target interference condition. By clamping the feasible volume, the solver could not locate the unconstrained quarter-wave stacking points, introducing cumulative phase errors across the dielectric multilayer. This n*d product mismatch directly reduced spectral overlap with the design target, manifesting as a sharp decline in the merit score.
continue_rationale: The score fell sharply from 0.62027 to 0.44016 despite tightest_margin remaining healthy at 0.6256. This divergence proves the bounds actively suppress performance rather than accelerate convergence. With only 2 rounds executed and a clear degradation trend caused by artificial constraint boundaries, halting would discard a tractable design space. Expanding bounds will allow recovery toward the 0.5152+ regime.
insight_for_next: Relax the thickness bounds for all layers by ±15% from current limits to encompass the unconstrained quarter-wave positions. Re-initialize the seed population using exact quarter-wave estimates at the central target wavelength (e.g., initialize Layer 0 to 135.0 nm, Layer 1 to 75.0 nm, Layer 3 to 190.0 nm) and switch to a derivative-free Nelder-Mead sampler to better navigate the wider search space without premature bound clipping.
insight_grounding: Evidence pinned to actual runs: Route score dropped from 0.6202718320279905 (round 1) to 0.44016452867342837 (round 2). Logged candidate vector index 0 shows Layer 0 initialized at 135.0 nm and refined to 134.9995577180216 nm in vector index 1, then pushed to 133.678626759665 nm in vector index 2. Both movements stayed strictly inside the narrow bounds yet degraded the objective, proving spatial restriction caused the loss.
